note: Curated first-party mods, fetched at runtime by TidePool. Editing this file changes what the Essentials tab shows without shipping a new app build - which is how a 'planned' entry becomes installable later.

mods.name: BepInEx (IL2CPP)
mods.summary: The mod loader. Install this first - almost every mod needs it.
mods.description:
BepInEx pack for IL2CPP x64 Unity games. Preconfigured and ready to use.

This is the loader that runs mods. Surf Sandbox has no official mod support, so nothing else here works without it - TidePool installs it into whichever profile you are using, so switching back to vanilla is always one click.

Pinned to 6.0.755, the build Thunderstore serves to every other IL2CPP game. Pinned rather than floating so a new upstream build cannot change what installs underneath you mid-session.

mods.name: SurfMP
mods.summary: Multiplayer for Surf Sandbox. Share a lineup with friends.
mods.description:
Adds multiplayer to Surf Sandbox: sit in the same lineup as your friends, watch each other take off, and trade waves.

The host runs the wave simulation and broadcasts it, so everyone is looking at the same ocean rather than hoping two machines drift to the same answer. Everything else - your surfer, your board, your position - is simulated locally and synced.

Uses Steam's peer-to-peer networking, so there is no port forwarding and no server to run. Invite through Steam and paddle out.

mods.name: Break Pack
mods.summary: Eight real waves, recreated from their actual sea-floor shape.
mods.description:
Pipeline, Teahupo'o, Nazare, Jeffreys Bay, Skeleton Bay, Mavericks, Puerto Escondido - and one gentle sandbar to learn on.

These are not drawn by eye. Each break is built from a cross-section of its real sea floor, because what a wave does is decided almost entirely by how fast the bottom rises underneath it. Teahupo'o goes from open ocean to half a metre of reef in about thirty metres, which is why it breaks below sea level. Skeleton Bay barely changes angle for a kilometre, which is why the rides never end.

The profiles are stylised rather than surveyed - they reproduce each wave's character, not navigational depths.

No loader needed: beaches are ordinary save files, so this installs and works without BepInEx.
